bug_description.original:
Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=6454671998582784

Project: coturn
Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer
Fuzz Target: FuzzStun
Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_coturn
Platform Id: linux

Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value
Crash Address: 
Crash State:
  stun_check_message_integrity_by_key_str
  stun_check_message_integrity_str
  FuzzStun.c
  
Sanitizer: memory (MSAN)

Recommended Security Severity: Medium
bug_description.normalized: In coturn's stun_check_message_integrity_str (ns_turn_msg.c:1971), the return value of strncpy (char *) is erroneously assigned to the size_t parameter len, corrupting the buffer length from its actual value to a stack address. When the corrupted length is passed to stun_check_message_integrity_by_key_str, the bounds check in stun_get_command_message_len_str is bypassed, allowing stun_attr_get_value to return a pointer whose 20-byte SHA1-sized window extends beyond the actual 28-byte buffer into uninitialized heap memory. The subsequent memcmp on this data triggers MemorySanitizer's use-of-uninitialized-value detection.

source.description: First project-code statement that parses the attacker-controlled STUN buffer, searching for a MESSAGE_INTEGRITY attribute using the corrupted buffer length. The attribute at offset 20 (type 0x0008, length 20) is found because the corrupted len makes the bounds check in stun_get_command_message_len_str vacuously pass.
source.value_from: The fuzz harness passes a crafted 28-byte STUN message buffer (Data, Size) from LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput to stun_check_message_integrity_str, which forwards buf and the corrupted len to this function; value buf; from stun_attr_get_first_by_type_str(buf, len, STUN_ATTRIBUTE_MESSAGE_INTEGRITY)

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: memcmp reads 20 bytes starting at old_hmac (buf + 24). The actual buffer is only 28 bytes, so the last 16 bytes of the 20-byte read extend into adjacent uninitialized heap memory, triggering MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.

root_cause.description: strncpy returns char * (the destination pointer pwd), but its return value is implicitly converted to size_t and assigned to len. This overwrites the caller-supplied buffer length with a stack address, corrupting len from its actual value (28) to a huge number (~0x7fff...).

tainted_value_origin.description: strncpy returns char * (destination pointer pwd), which is implicitly cast to size_t and assigned to len, corrupting the buffer length parameter that controls all subsequent bounds checking.

fine_trace.note: strncpy returns char * (destination pointer pwd), not size_t. The implicit pointer-to-integer conversion assigns the stack address of pwd to len, overwriting the actual buffer length (28) with a value like 0x7fff.... pwd itself is correctly populated with upwd and null-terminated at line 1972.

Searches the attacker-controlled STUN buffer for a MESSAGE_INTEGRITY attribute (type 0x0008). Inside stun_get_command_message_len_str (line 396-397), the header-claimed body length (24) plus header (20) = 44 is checked against the corrupted len; since 44 < ~0x7fff..., the check passes and bufLen=44 is accepted. The PoC has a MESSAGE_INTEGRITY attribute at byte offset 20 with length 20 (SHA1SIZEBYTES), which stun_attr_check_valid accepts within the 24-byte remaining window.

fine_trace.code: res = stun_calculate_hmac(buf, (size_t)new_len - 4 - shasize, pwd, strlen((char *)pwd), new_hmac, &shasize, shatype);
fine_trace.note: Computes HMAC-SHA1 over the first 20 bytes of buf using pwd as the key. orig_len (44, from stun_get_command_message_len_str at line 1929 using corrupted len) and sar position yield new_len = 20 + 4 + 20 = 44. The HMAC covers (size_t)(44 - 4 - 20) = 20 bytes of buf. Result is written to new_hmac[20].

Extracts a pointer to the attribute value: old_hmac = sar + 4 = buf + 24. The attribute's declared length is 20 bytes (SHA1), so the expected read window is buf[24..43]. The actual buffer is only 28 bytes, so only buf[24..27] (4 bytes: ff ff 00 00) are within the allocation; buf[28..43] (16 bytes) lie in adjacent heap memory allocated by OPENSSL_LH_insert via malloc, which MSAN marks as uninitialized.

Compares 20 bytes of old_hmac against new_hmac. At offset 8 within old_hmac (buf + 32, four bytes beyond the buffer end), memcmp reads uninitialized heap bytes, triggering MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from ARVO vulnerable Docker sanitizer_trace.txt

format.name: STUN binary message
format.contract: 28-byte binary blob encoding a STUN-like message with a MESSAGE_INTEGRITY attribute (type 0x0008) at byte offset 20 with declared length 20 (SHA1SIZEBYTES), and a header-claimed body length of 24 exceeding the actual 8 bytes of body. The input must be between 10 and 5120 bytes to pass the harness size check, and stun_check_message_integrity_str must be called with ct=TURN_CREDENTIALS_SHORT_TERM so the strncpy return-type bug corrupts len.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC passes the harness size check (28 bytes is within 10-5120) and is admitted into the SHORT_TERM credential branch of stun_check_message_integrity_str, where the strncpy type confusion corrupts len.
